evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never delivered the 10-15 minute time-box + dependable quote framing; jumped straight into profile/discovery questions.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving day (Wednesday the 30th), approximate size (6000 sq ft but only partial items), some items mentioned (king bed, China hutch, chairs) early. Name (Brenda Schnurbusch) and phone (214-801-2870) gathered late.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: 6000 sq ft home identified; no virtual walkthrough offered despite meeting the 1,800+ sq ft threshold for Section 1's walkthrough branch.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (large home in The Woodlands), floor layout (upstairs/downstairs), parking/access (can pull under portico, side/front door entry), detailed item list (king bed, armoire, China hutch, 4 leather chairs, sofa, ottoman, granite coffee table, bar stools, foosball table, air hockey table, tall lamp, large pictures, foyer table), special consideration (items going to storage unit, climate-controlled, wrapping for protection).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes: 'we can also do packing. We can pack as many as well as you want.'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not in the standard form; rep did not ask typical box count / overflow check. Customer offered '4 to 6 boxes' for glassware/bar items in response to packing discussion, but rep did not proactively ask about typical home box count.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave an estimate ($1,460 for 5 hours, 2.5-hour minimum + hourly rate of $210/hour + $150 trip fee + ~$300 packing supplies) but did not anchor it to a typical range for a home this size before personalizing.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Rep stated hourly rate ($210/hour), 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increments ($51-52 per increment), and disclosed trip fee ($150) and packing supply estimate (~$300). Did not mention overnight fee or fully frame the 'not a guess' / commitment language around the estimate.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep gave estimate and transitioned immediately to checking on window availability and storage address; no pause or 'Does that feel fair?' check for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. The Two Promises section (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) was entirely skipped; no version of 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closure was delivered.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moved straight to sending confirmation email without asking a genuine final-concerns check like 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was not asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Yes, implicit. Rep said 'go ahead and book it' in response to customer's 'okay, so yeah, go ahead and book it,' confirming the booking. The explicit ask was not initiated plainly by the rep—the customer offered it first.

top_strength: Thorough and detailed inventory capture — the rep systematically documented every furniture item, special consideration (storage wrapping, climate control), and packing need, then read it back to confirm accuracy.
coaching_note: Skip the entire opening time-box and dependability framing, and critical discovery and Two Promises sections were completely omitted; rework your call flow to follow the seven-section card in order before moving to estimate, especially for moves ≥1,800 sq ft that may route to a virtual walkthrough instead.
